concepts.title: Meaning and Importance of Local Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Importance of Local Government' refers to.
questions.a: Local government is the government at the village, town, or city level, closest to the people, responsible for addressing local needs and providing basic services, and considered essential for a genuine democracy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Importance of Local Government'.
questions.a: Local government brings democracy closer to the people by allowing citizens to participate directly in decision-making on matters that affect their daily lives.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning and Importance of Local Government' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Why Local Government?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Panchayati Raj System' refers to.
questions.a: The Panchayati Raj system is the three-tier structure of rural local self-government in India, consisting of the Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level, given constitutional status by the 73rd Amendment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Panchayati Raj System'.
questions.a: The Panchayati Raj system institutionalises grassroots democracy in rural India through a three-tier structure that brings governance and decision-making to the village, block, and district levels.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Panchayati Raj System' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Panchayati Raj System

concepts.title: Three-Tier Structure: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Three-Tier Structure: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad' refers to.
questions.a: The three tiers of the Panchayati Raj are the Gram Panchayat at the village level, elected by the Gram Sabha; the Panchayat Samiti at the block level, coordinating the work of Gram Panchayats; and the Zila Parishad at the district level, the apex body overseeing district-wide planning.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Three-Tier Structure: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad'.
questions.a: Each tier of the Panchayati Raj has a distinct role and jurisdiction, with the higher tiers coordinating and supporting the work of the lower tiers in a linked structure of rural local governance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Three-Tier Structure: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Three Tiers of Panchayati Raj

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Municipal Corporations and Municipalities' refers to.
questions.a: Urban local government in India is carried out by Municipal Corporations in large cities and Municipalities (Municipal Councils or Nagar Panchayats) in smaller towns, responsible for civic services and urban development, given constitutional status by the 74th Amendment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Municipal Corporations and Municipalities'.
questions.a: Urban local government provides essential civic services and infrastructure in cities and towns through elected bodies, with Municipal Corporations for big cities and Municipalities for smaller urban areas.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Municipal Corporations and Municipalities' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Urban Local Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what '73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments' refers to.
questions.a: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) gave constitutional status to rural local government (Panchayati Raj) by adding Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule, while the 74th Amendment gave constitutional status to urban local government by adding Part IX-A and the Twelfth Schedule, both mandating regular elections and reservations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about '73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments'.
questions.a: The 73rd and 74th Amendments transformed local government from a state-level arrangement into a constitutionally mandated tier of governance, ensuring regular elections, reservations for women and marginalised groups, and devolution of powers.

questions.q: Under which section is '73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 73rd and 74th Amendments

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Functions of Local Government' refers to.
questions.a: The functions of local government include providing basic civic services like water supply, sanitation, street lighting, and maintenance of local roads; implementing welfare and development schemes; and ensuring public health and local planning, as listed in the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Functions of Local Government'.
questions.a: Local governments perform the essential day-to-day functions that directly affect citizens' lives, from basic civic services to the implementation of development schemes, making them the most visible level of government.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Functions of Local Government' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Functions of Local Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Decentralisation' refers to.
questions.a: Decentralisation is the process of transferring power and authority from higher levels of government to lower levels, especially to local governments, so that decisions are made closer to the people affected by them.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Decentralisation'.
questions.a: Decentralisation is the principle of taking decision-making power closer to the people, making government more responsive, participatory, and accountable at the grassroots level.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Decentralisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Decentralisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Challenges to Local Government' refers to.
questions.a: The major challenges to local government in India include insufficient devolution of funds and powers, interference by state governments, lack of capacity and resources, irregular elections in some states, and the domination of local elites over Panchayat institutions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Challenges to Local Government'.
questions.a: Despite constitutional recognition, local governments in India face practical challenges of inadequate funds, limited powers, state interference, and elite capture, which weaken their effectiveness as institutions of grassroots democracy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Challenges to Local Government' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Challenges to Local Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Elections and Reservations in Local Government' refers to.
questions.a: Local government elections are conducted every five years by an independent State Election Commission, with seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women (at least one-third, and in many states one-half), to ensure inclusive representation at the grassroots level.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Elections and Reservations in Local Government'.
questions.a: Regular elections and reservations in local government ensure democratic accountability and the representation of women and marginalised communities, making grassroots democracy inclusive and participatory.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Elections and Reservations in Local Government' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Elections and Reservations in Local Bodies
